topics.title: Supreme Court keeps mail voting rules
topics.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected an effort to restrict mail-in voting before the midterms, leaving state voting procedures in place.
topics.discussionPrompt: If voting rules become the day’s argument, who trusts the mailbox and who immediately wants a laminated flowchart?

topics.title: AI regulation debate keeps building
topics.summary: Washington’s AI debate intensified as some leaders urged stronger safeguards, while the White House argued regulation could slow U.S. competitiveness.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a tool gets powerful enough to make everyone nervous and excited, who says ‘slow down’ and who asks to try it first?

topics.title: Gates Foundation backs inclusive AI
topics.summary: The Gates Foundation pledged $1 billion to expand AI access in health, education, agriculture, and language tools for underserved communities.
topics.discussionPrompt: If AI help finally reaches places that usually get tech last, who celebrates first and who asks how they’ll know it actually works?

topics.title: Markets watch oil and rates
topics.summary: Global markets stayed uneasy as oil prices, bond yields, central-bank expectations, and AI-stock worries shaped investor mood.
topics.discussionPrompt: When oil, interest rates, and tech stocks all walk into the same conversation, who pretends to understand the chart?

topics.title: NATO responds to Baltic drone
topics.summary: NATO jets shot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace, while Denmark reported a tense encounter involving a Russian warship and a helicopter.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the neighborhood watch suddenly involves fighter jets, who wants calm facts and who starts moving chairs away from the windows?

topics.title: US says drone boat was protected
topics.summary: The U.S. military said it destroyed two small Iranian boats that tried to seize an unmanned American sea drone near Iranian waters.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a robot boat causes an international incident, who asks what it was doing there and who wants to name it?

topics.title: Apple enters foldable phone race
topics.summary: Apple unveiled its first folding handset, adding a major new competitor to a phone category that rivals have been testing for years.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your phone folds like a tiny laptop, who calls it genius and who worries about sitting on it wrong?

topics.title: UK nations press constitutional change
topics.summary: Nationalist leaders from Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland called for Westminster to allow clearer paths toward constitutional change.
topics.discussionPrompt: When several roommates ask to renegotiate the house rules at once, who brings history and who brings snacks?

topics.title: Pokemon fans await big reveal
topics.summary: Pokemon fans prepared for what BBC described as one of the franchise’s biggest days in years, with major announcements expected.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a fandom says today is enormous, who queues up calmly and who has already made three theories before breakfast?

topics.title: Canada extortion crackdown continues
topics.summary: Canada deported four more Indian nationals in an extortion-linked immigration crackdown, bringing reported removals in the operation to 111.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a crime story turns into a cross-border paperwork story too, who follows the case and who asks how communities rebuild trust?
